title: Uniformly bounded algebraic coordinates in a countable-dimensional ultrametric space
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with its extended nonarchimedean norm [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V\ne0$ be an $E$-vector space with a norm satisfying $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$ and $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$, with $\|v\|=0$ precisely for $v=0$. Suppose $V$ is spanned algebraically by a finite or countable sequence; no completeness of $V$ is assumed. For any prescribed $v_0\ne0$ there is an algebraic basis $(b_j)_{j\in J}$ (every vector has a unique finite linear expansion) with $0\in J$, $b_0=v_0$, where $J$ is either $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ for some $d\geq1$ or $\mathbf N$, and constants $0<c\leq C<\infty$ such that for every finitely supported family $(a_j)$ in $E$,
$$c\max_j|a_j|\leq\Big\|\sum_ja_jb_j\Big\|\leq C\max_j|a_j|.$$
The maximum of the empty support is zero. In particular every coordinate projection, every projection onto an arbitrary subset of $J$, and every linear map sending the basis bijectively onto a subset of itself are continuous. The inverse from that coordinate subspace onto $V$ is continuous when the subset is in bijection with $J$. These are algebraic finite-support coordinates, not an assertion about infinite series.
